Nathan
/NAY-thun/
proper noun
Hebrew Natan — he has given. Several men bear the name; the prophet Nathan is the giver of the LORD’s word to David — house, sin, and succession.

Biblical Definition

Nathan the prophet stands in David’s court as the LORD’s mouth. The king said unto Nathan that he dwelt in a house of cedar while the ark dwelt within curtains (2Sa 7:2). Nathan later said unto David, Thou art the man, after the LORD had anointed him and delivered him from Saul (2Sa 12:7). In the succession crisis he is listed with Zadok among those not with Adonijah (1Ki 1:8). A true prophet gives the word even when the king has cedar and blood on his hands.

Key Scripture

2 Samuel 7:2 — "That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains."

2 Samuel 12:7 — "And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;"

1 Kings 1:8 — "But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David, were not with Adonijah."

Modern Corruption

The age wants a court chaplain who blesses cedar and stays out of adultery. Nathan’s office is “Thou art the man,” not palace wellness.

expand to see more

Religious professionals are hired to soothe powerful men. Nathan is not hired that way in the text. He hears the king’s building impulse and later names the king’s sin. Gifted speech without that courage is not this name.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Natan — he has given. The prophet is given to David as word, not as accessory.

expand to see more

Hebrew Natan — he has given.

Prophet in the cedar-and-curtains conversation (2Sa 7:2).

“Thou art the man” as the LORD’s given sentence (2Sa 12:7).

Usage

"Nathan gives the LORD’s word to the king, including accusation."

"Cedar houses do not silence the prophet."

"Do not hire a Nathan who will not say Thou art the man."
